name: blood-vasculature-network
title: Blood Vasculature Network — VCCF transport graph to couple organ models
question:
Can the HRA/VCCF vasculature data define a whole-body blood-transport
network — a directed heart -> organ -> heart circuit through named vessels —
that we can use to COUPLE independent organ simulations by advecting shared
blood-borne solutes (glucose, O2, insulin, ...) between them? And what does a
v1 blood-circulation simulation over that network look like?

study_card.goal: Pull the VCCF vasculature data, build + validate a directed whole-body blood-transport graph, and design the blood-circulation simulation that will run organ models as nodes on it.
study_card.mechanism: VasculatureNetworkStep.update -> vascular_network_summary(): load the 28 FTU heart->FTU->heart paths (FTU_Table_S1) + VCCF vessel classes (hra-vccf Vessel.csv), build a directed vessel graph (nodes=vessels/chambers/FTUs, edges=consecutive path steps), and check every FTU closes a circuit through a heart chamber -> RAMEmitter.
study_card.expected_result: A connected directed graph: 28 FTU circuits, ~191 vessels, ~444 flow edges, split into artery/capillary/vein/chamber classes, with every FTU route starting AND ending at a heart chamber (a closed circuit).
study_card.main_expert_question: Is the FTU-path topology (28 curated heart->FTU->heart routes) the right substrate to couple organ models, or do we need the finer VCCF Vessel.csv `BranchesFrom` tree (1082 vessels) to capture shared trunks / branch-point mixing where flows merge?

biological_summary:
Organ models in this atlas (glucose regulation across liver/pancreas/muscle,
the FTU digital objects, the biomodel corpus) are currently islands — each
simulates one tissue with no physical connection to the others. In the body
they are coupled by BLOOD: the heart drives a closed circuit that carries
metabolites and signals from organ to organ, so a change in hepatic glucose
output reaches the pancreatic beta-cell through the vasculature, with a
transport delay set by the path length and flow rate.

This study establishes the missing connective substrate. The HRA/VCCF
vasculature data gives, for each of 28 functional tissue units, an ordered
vessel path from a heart chamber out to the FTU's exchange capillary and back
(arterial steps toward the FTU, venous steps returning) — e.g. the alveolus
runs right ventricle -> pulmonary trunk -> ... -> alveolar capillary -> ... ->
left atrium. Taking the union over all 28 FTUs yields a directed whole-body
transport graph. On top of it, a blood-circulation simulation advects a shared
plasma solute vector along the edges (a flow/resistance model sets the rates),
and each organ node is an existing organ Process that exchanges solutes with
the blood it is perfused by — turning a set of isolated organ models into one
coupled, circulating whole.
readouts: ftu_routes[FTU] — the ordered heart -> FTU -> heart vessel path a solute travels

report.title: Blood Vasculature Network — 28 closed FTU circuits, 191 vessels, 444 flow edges (v1 topology)
report.objective:
Turn the HRA/VCCF vasculature data into a validated directed blood-transport
graph, and design the circulation simulation that will couple organ models
as nodes on it.
report.conclusion:
The data-pull runs and validates. From FTU_Table_S1 (28 FTUs) plus the VCCF
vessel classes, VasculatureNetworkStep builds a directed graph of 191
vessels and 444 flow edges — 94 arteries, 73 veins, 20 exchange capillaries,
4 heart chambers — and every one of the 28 FTU routes is a CLOSED circuit:
it starts at a heart chamber and returns to one (n_closed_circuits = 28,
n_open_routes = 0). So the vasculature data is sufficient to define a
coherent whole-body transport topology to hang organ models on. The
blood-circulation simulation itself is designed in
docs/blood-circulation-simulation-plan.md and is NOT yet implemented.
report.caveat:
This study delivers the TOPOLOGY and the plan only — no flow dynamics or
solute transport are simulated yet (simulation_status "ran" refers to the
data-pull/graph composite, not a circulation run). The graph is built from
the 28 curated FTU paths; it does not yet model branch-point mixing where
flows merge (that needs the finer VCCF Vessel.csv `BranchesFrom` tree), nor
per-edge flow rates (Q), which the plan assigns from a hemodynamic model.

findings.statement:
The VCCF data yields a fully closed whole-body transport graph: all 28
FTU routes start and end at a heart chamber (28 closed circuits, 0 open),
spanning 191 vessels and 444 directed flow edges (94 artery / 20
capillary / 73 vein / 4 chamber). The topology substrate for coupling
organ models is therefore complete and validated.

A blood-circulation simulation is designed on this graph (see
docs/blood-circulation-simulation-plan.md): a BloodTransportProcess
advects a shared plasma solute vector along the edges at flow rates Q set
by a hemodynamic model (resistance network or the Font-Clos 2020
cardiac-output partition), and each organ node is an existing organ
Process exchanging solutes with the blood perfusing it. Glucose
regulation (liver <-> pancreas <-> muscle) is the proposed first coupling.
findings.evidence: Design doc + the Font-Clos et al. 2020 whole-body organ-flow-network precedent (references/papers.bib).

limitations: Topology only — no flow rates or solute transport simulated yet.
Uses the 28 curated FTU paths; branch-point mixing (shared trunks) needs the VCCF Vessel.csv BranchesFrom tree.
Vessel geometry (radii/lengths in vccf/Geometry.csv) not yet used to parameterize resistances.
discovery_implications:
Establishes the blood-transport network as the connective substrate that lets
this atlas's organ models stop being islands: with per-edge flow and a shared
plasma compartment, a change in one organ's solute exchange propagates to the
others with a physiologically-ordered transport delay. Next: implement the
BloodTransportProcess and couple the glucose-regulation organ models as the
first circulating multi-organ composite.

assumptions: The graph is built from the 28 curated FTU heart->FTU->heart paths (FTU_Table_S1); branch-point mixing where flows merge is NOT modeled and would need the finer VCCF Vessel.csv BranchesFrom tree.
Per-edge flow rates (Q) and vessel geometry (radii/lengths) are not yet used -- the plan assigns Q from a hemodynamic model, unimplemented here.
A valid transport substrate requires every FTU route to close a circuit through a heart chamber; open routes would indicate missing vessel data.

alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: all 28 FTU routes close a circuit through a heart chamber (0 open routes), so the data IS sufficient for a coherent directed transport graph.

alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: it does not -- the curated FTU paths omit branch-point mixing; capturing it needs the VCCF Vessel.csv BranchesFrom tree (stated limitation).
